course_title: Business Process Automation with Power Automate and Copilot Studio Agents
deck: Business Process Automation with Power Automate and Copilot Studio Agents-v8.2.pptx
design_principle: Concepts first, labs second. Every lab is preceded by the concept slides that explain it, and every concept slide names the lab where it is applied.
naming_rule: Workflows in the tenant are named exactly as the lab title ('Lab N - <Title>'); agents are named 'Lab N - <Agent Name>' (e.g. 'Lab 5 - HR Agent'); helper workflows and every artefact carry the lab prefix ('Lab 6 - Raise Requisition', 'Lab 2 - Enquiry Log.xlsx', 'Lab 12 - Customers'). Agent names are capped at 30 characters by Copilot Studio, so learners use e.g. 'Lab 9 - Marketing Manager' (25). The trainer's canonical workflows AND agents both carry the suffix ' (DO NOT DELETE)'; agent base names are shortened to fit the 30-character cap (e.g. 'Lab 5 - HR (DO NOT DELETE)', 'Lab 6 - Proc (DO NOT DELETE)', 'Lab 9 - Mgr (DO NOT DELETE)'); learners name their own builds plainly. Every hands-on build uses the Copilot Studio new-experience designer; classic Power Automate is never opened.

labs.title: Lab 0 — Environment Setup
labs.subtitle: Training Class Sandbox (assigned by your trainer)
labs.platform: Power Platform admin centre + Copilot Studio
labs.teaches: One Training Class Sandbox, with Dataverse and Copilot Credits, stands behind every later lab — and one designer builds everything.

labs.title: Lab 1 — Trigger and Actions
labs.subtitle: Form to email confirmation
labs.platform: Copilot Studio workflow + Microsoft Forms + Outlook
labs.teaches: A trigger starts a workflow; connector actions consume the trigger's outputs as dynamic content.

labs.title: Lab 2 — Log to Excel
labs.subtitle: Log the enquiry, then send the email
labs.teaches: Commit before you confirm — the audit row is written before the acknowledgement is sent.

labs.title: Lab 3 — Leave Application Approval
labs.subtitle: The workflow pauses for a manager
labs.teaches: A running workflow suspends at the approval action and branches with If/Else on the human decision.

labs.title: Lab 4 — Email Classification
labs.subtitle: An inbox workflow that sorts, replies, books and escalates
labs.platform: Copilot Studio workflow + Outlook + Classify + Human review + Teams
labs.teaches: The Classify node sorts each email into five categories; each port runs a deterministic handler, and the Priority branch stops at a human in Teams.

labs.title: Lab 5 — Your First Agent
labs.subtitle: An HR agent: instructions, knowledge, test, publish
labs.teaches: An agent is instructions plus a model plus knowledge — and the Preview tab is where you find out what it will refuse.

labs.title: Lab 6 — Procurement Agent with Tools
labs.subtitle: A workflow as a tool, and the audit row it writes
labs.platform: Copilot Studio agent + workflow as a tool + Excel Online
labs.teaches: The agent decides a tool applies and fills its inputs; the workflow's own logic is enforced — and the reference number it returns is the proof it ran.

labs.title: Lab 7 — Sales Agent with Knowledge
labs.subtitle: Grounded in 20 brochures, and refusing to invent
labs.teaches: Grounding is giving the agent facts and taking away every other source — a public-facing agent whose worst failure is an invented fee.

labs.title: Lab 8 — IT Support Agent with Skills
labs.subtitle: Five uploaded skill packages, and the one rule none of them can enforce
labs.teaches: A skill is a procedure the model decides to apply, not a permission — and a tool the agent does not have is a control.
labs.path: labs/Lab 8 - IT Support Agent with Skills/index.md

labs.title: Lab 9 — Multi-Agent Content Team
labs.subtitle: Manager, Research, Blog and Review — one pipeline, four agents, and a human at the end
labs.teaches: One topic, four agents: the manager owns the conversation and delegates by stage of work — and nothing is final until a person approves.

labs.title: Lab 10 — Calling Agent from Workflow
labs.subtitle: Blog-writer workflow: topic in, Teams post out
labs.platform: Copilot Studio workflow + M365 Copilot + Teams
labs.teaches: The workflow calls the model at a fixed step, then acts on the result deterministically.

labs.title: Lab 11 — Calling Workflow from Agent
labs.subtitle: A blog-writer agent that calls a workflow as its tool
labs.platform: Copilot Studio agent + workflow as a tool
labs.teaches: The mirror image of Lab 10: the agent decides when to call the workflow, and the flow's inputs and outputs are the contract it programs against.

labs.title: Lab 12 — HTTP and Application Approval Agent
labs.subtitle: Marina Trust Bank customer onboarding
labs.teaches: The boundary of agency — the AI decides what to do; deterministic actions do what must always happen.
labs.path: labs/Lab 12 - HTTP and Application Approval Agent/index.md
tenant_names: Lab 12 - HTTP and Application Approval Agent

labs.title: Lab 13 — HTTP and Chatbot
labs.subtitle: Investment advisor chatbot
labs.platform: Copilot Studio workflow + SharePoint knowledge + website
labs.teaches: The agent alone — rules in the instruction, facts in the knowledge source, and a refusal it must never break.

labs.title: Lab 14 — HTTP and Human Review
labs.subtitle: Client rapport assistant with a Teams approval gate
labs.platform: Copilot Studio workflow + Human review + Excel Online + Teams
labs.teaches: Human in the loop — the AI drafts, and the workflow physically cannot proceed until a person approves.

labs.title: Lab 15 — RAG with Knowledge Base
labs.subtitle: Cook & Bake Academy, built-in knowledge
labs.teaches: RAG as a product setting — three nodes, no ingestion, and nothing you can inspect.

labs.title: Lab 16 — RAG with Pinecone
labs.subtitle: The same chatbot, with the levers back
labs.teaches: What the convenience cost — chunking, embeddings, dimension and top_k, back in your hands.

labs.title: Lab 17 — Publish to Teams, Microsoft 365 Copilot and the Web
labs.subtitle: Channels + — where a published agent meets its users
labs.platform: Copilot Studio Channels + Microsoft Teams + Microsoft 365 Copilot + website
labs.teaches: Publish is what channels serve; each channel needs something different, and none of them changes the agent — a channel is a door, not a brain.
